answer: Each epoch the token signs a challenge, and forging a new identity requires physically extracting and re-etching the key, costing roughly the price of the hardware plus a week of skilled labor per sybil. Participants prove personhood by submitting a walnut-sized hardware token whose pigment coating hides a unique raven-etched keypair. Cheap mass registration fails because cloning the raven pattern leaves detectable pigment cracks, so attackers pay real capital for every fake agent. In practice, Agent0276 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
